meta.titre: Informal Letter: following the task, keeping the tone and setting it out
meta.sous_theme: Layout, tone and developing each point

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: When a cousin in Kumba hears that you have passed an exam, you do not send a stiff official message. You write or call and speak warmly, with news, thanks and advice. In Paper 2 the informal letter asks for exactly this, but in writing and in good English. The question gives you your name, your address and the name of the person, so the marks are won by following each instruction, keeping a friendly but correct tone, and setting the letter out clearly. This course shows you how.

items: A paragraph deals with one main idea and begins on a new line.
A formal letter uses "Dear Sir" and "Yours faithfully"; a letter to a friend or relative is different.
Names, places and the first word of a sentence begin with a capital letter.

sections.titre: Writing an informal letter that follows the task
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Layout

| Part | What to write |
|---|---|
| Sender's address | In the top right corner: the address given in the question, for example P.O. Box 55, Ndop |
| Date | Under the address |
| Salutation | *Dear* + the first name of the receiver + a comma, for example *Dear Che,* |
| Opening paragraph | A greeting, a wish for good health and the reason for writing |
| Body | One paragraph for each instruction in the question |
| Closing paragraph | A short wish, greetings to the family and a request for a reply |
| Ending | *Yours lovingly,* or *Your friend,* followed by your first name |

An informal letter has no address for the receiver. Use the name and the address given in the question and do not invent others.

### Read the task first

Underline each instruction (verbs such as *thank, congratulate, advise, tell, convince, say what you plan*). Each one is a point of the plan, and each point is a paragraph. If you forget one, you lose marks for content.

### Tone and language

Write like a warm and respectful person talking: *I was so glad to hear...* Short forms such as *I'm* suit a friendly tone, but avoid slang, text-message spelling (*u, pls, 2day*) and very long, formal sentences. The grammar, spelling and punctuation must still be correct.

### How it is marked

In general, examiners reward **content** (all the points of the task, well developed), **expression** (clear paragraphs, suitable tone, varied sentences) and **accuracy** (spelling, punctuation, grammar). Leave time to read the letter again.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the task says, for example, to thank or congratulate and then to give plans, advice or news
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give each task its own paragraph in the order of the question. Open with the first task (thanks or congratulations) with real details, then change paragraph for the second (plans or advice). Use link words such as *First, Second, Finally* for several pieces of advice.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must convince someone to change a decision, such as returning to school
variantes.contenu_markdown: Show that you understand the other person's situation. Then give two or three reasons (for example, better chances of work, independence and the chance to help the family). Answer a likely objection, such as cost or shame, and offer your help. End kindly, because a friendly tone persuades better than a harsh one.

variantes.nom: Letter to an older relative or guardian
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the receiver is an uncle, an aunt or a guardian
variantes.contenu_markdown: Keep the warm tone but add respect: *Dear Uncle Joe,* and phrases such as *I am grateful for everything you have done for me*. Do not use slang. Be specific about what you thank the person for and what you promise to do.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write a letter to your cousin, who lives in Bafoussam, congratulating him on winning a scholarship and advising him on how to use the opportunity. Your name is Bih, your address is P.O. Box 55, Ndop, and your cousin's name is Che.

etapes.action: Read the task and underline the instructions.
etapes.justification: There are two instructions: congratulate and advise. The form is an informal letter, and the names and address are given.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Sender: Bih, P.O. Box 55, Ndop. Receiver: Che. Tasks: congratulate; advise.

etapes.justification: Each instruction needs its own paragraph, with a short opening and a short closing.
etapes.resultat_markdown: P1 opening; P2 congratulations; P3 three pieces of advice; P4 closing wishes.

etapes.action: Set out the heading and salutation.
etapes.justification: The given address goes top right, followed by a date; the salutation uses the first name and a comma.
etapes.resultat_markdown: P.O. Box 55, Ndop. 3 June. Dear Che,

etapes.justification: Details such as the evenings spent studying make the praise believable, and linking words make the advice clear.
A friendly ending and your first name complete the letter. Check punctuation, spelling and tenses.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
A model letter follows.

> P.O. Box 55,
> Ndop.
> 3 June
>
> Dear Che,
>
> How are you? I hope that you and the family are in good health. I am very well, and I am writing with great joy because Mum told me your wonderful news.
>
> Congratulations on winning the scholarship! I am so proud of you. All the evenings you spent studying while the rest of us were playing have finally paid off. Everybody at home is celebrating, and Grandma has even promised to cook your favourite dish.
>
> Now I would like to give you some advice so that you make the best of this chance. First, keep the study habits that brought you this success, and ask your teachers for help whenever you do not understand something. Second, manage your time carefully, because new friends and new places can be a distraction. Finally, look after your health and stay in touch with your family.
>
> I wish you every success, and I look forward to hearing from you soon. Please give my greetings to your parents.
>
> Yours lovingly,
> Bih

items.erreur_markdown: Starting with "Dear Sir," and ending with "Yours faithfully" in a letter to a cousin.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are formal phrases. An informal letter begins with the first name and ends with a friendly phrase.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the name "Mary" and a made-up address when the question gives the writer's name and address.
items.pourquoi_faux: The task gives these details, and a different name or address ignores the instruction.
items.correction_markdown: Use the name and the address exactly as the question gives them.

items.erreur_markdown: Thanking the person for the help but saying nothing about the plans, when the question asks for both.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each part of the task earns marks for content. A missing part loses them.
items.correction_markdown: Write one paragraph for the thanks and one for the plans.

items.erreur_markdown: "Hw r u? I hope u r fine. Pls write bk 2 me."
items.pourquoi_faux: Text-message spelling is not acceptable in an examination, even in a friendly letter.
items.correction_markdown: How are you? I hope you are fine. Please write back to me.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing the whole letter as one block with no paragraphs.
items.pourquoi_faux: The reader cannot see the separate points, and expression marks are lost.
items.correction_markdown: Begin a new paragraph for the opening, each point of the task and the closing.

items.enonce_markdown: Put these parts of a letter in the usual order: (a) the body of the letter, (b) Dear Ayem, (c) Yours lovingly, Ngu, (d) P.O. Box 12, Wum, and the date, (e) a closing sentence asking for a reply, (f) the opening greeting and the reason for writing.
items.solution_markdown: The order is **d, b, f, a, e, c**: address and date, salutation, opening, body, closing sentence, ending with the name.

items.enonce_markdown:
Read this task: *Write a letter to your aunt thanking her for the school bag she sent you for your birthday, and telling her how you will use it. Your name is Nji, your address is P.O. Box 7, Mbengwi, and your aunt's name is Lum.*

(a) List the two points of the plan.

(b) Write the heading and the salutation.

(c) Write the opening paragraph (three or four sentences).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Point 1: thank her for the bag. Point 2: say how you will use it.**

(b) **P.O. Box 7, Mbengwi.** then a date, then **Dear Aunt Lum,**

(c) Model: *I hope you are in good health and that everything is going well at home. I am very well and the new term has begun. I am writing to thank you for the lovely school bag that you sent me for my birthday.*

Award a mark for each: a greeting, the reason for writing, a friendly tone, correct tenses and spelling.

items.enonce_markdown: Your friend Neba lives in another town and is discouraged after failing a mock exam. Write a letter to Neba encouraging him and saying what he should do to improve. Your name is Ful and your address is P.O. Box 81, Tubah. Write three or four paragraphs.
items.solution_markdown:
Model letter:

P.O. Box 81,
Tubah.
20 July

Dear Neba,

I hope this letter finds you in good health. I was sorry to hear about your result in the mock exam, and I am writing to cheer you up.

Please do not lose heart. One failed test does not decide your future, and many people fail a test at some point and still succeed later.

First, look at your paper carefully and find out where you lost marks. Then make a timetable and study a little every day. If a subject is difficult, ask a teacher or a classmate to help you. Finally, take care of yourself by sleeping well and eating well.

I believe in you. Write to me soon and tell me how your new timetable is working.

Your friend,
Ful

Award a mark for each of these points: correct layout with the given address and salutation; one paragraph each for the opening, the encouragement and the advice; at least three practical pieces of advice; a friendly and correct tone; an ending with the writer's first name; and correct spelling and punctuation.

items_markdown: Set out the letter with the given address, a date, "Dear + first name,", paragraphs, a friendly ending and your first name.
Underline every instruction in the task and give each one its own paragraph.
Use the names and the address that the question gives; do not invent others.
The tone is warm and natural, but the grammar, spelling and punctuation must be correct (no text-message spelling).
Content, expression and accuracy are all marked, so leave time to read your letter again.
